question: What did we see in this patient that nobody has described before?

gagnier2013.cite: Gagnier et al. (2013). The CARE guidelines: consensus-based clinical case reporting guideline development. Journal of Medical Case Reports 7: 223.
gagnier2013.checked: every quote read word for word in the Europe PMC full text (PMC3844611) on 20 Nov 2026; the article is online-only, so places are given as its sections and CARE checklist items (Table 1); in-text reference numbers are left out. The card's own reference, the CARE explanation and elaboration (Riley et al. 2017), is not open access and was not read

steps.title: Notice
steps.text: A clinician meets a patient whose illness, or response to treatment, does not fit what is known. That surprise is the reason to write.

quotes.text: They have proved helpful in the identification of adverse and beneficial effects, the recognition of new diseases, unusual forms of common diseases, and the presentation of rare diseases

steps.title: Describe
steps.text: Write down who the patient is, what they complained of, their history and what the examination found, in enough detail that a reader could recognise the next one.

quotes.text: A case report is a detailed narrative that describes, for medical, scientific, or educational purposes, a medical problem experienced by one or several patients
Main symptoms of the patient (his or her chief complaints)

steps.title: Timeline
steps.text: Put the events in date order: onset, tests, treatments, follow-up. Order matters, because readers will ask what came before what.

quotes.text: The timeline should show how the key events of the case unfolded.

steps.title: Diagnose and treat
steps.text: Say how the diagnosis was reached, which others were considered and ruled out, and what was given, at what dose and for how long.

quotes.text: Diagnostic reasoning including other diagnoses considered
Administration of intervention (eg, dosage, strength, duration)

steps.title: Follow up
steps.text: Report what happened at every follow-up visit, good and bad, including events nobody expected.

steps.title: Raise a hypothesis
steps.text: Discuss what the case might mean and why, then hand it on: one case can suggest a cause, but only a study with a comparison can test it.

quotes.text: Case reports may generate hypotheses for future clinical studies
The rationale for conclusions (including assessments of cause and effect)

limits: The page follows the 2013 CARE statement, not the card's reference (Riley et al. 2017, the explanation and elaboration), which is behind a paywall and was not read.
The 1981 MMWR report on Pneumocystis pneumonia named on the card was not read for this page; no detail of it is shown.
The step texts in our own words are summaries of the quotes beside them; the quotes are the authority.
English only for now; the learn pages are not in the i18n pipeline yet.
